Subject: RFP questionnaire — clarifications on GPU mix and phased reservations

Hi Ben,

Thanks for confirming you received our RFP. A couple of clarifications from our infra and procurement teams as we start filling the vendor questionnaire:

- We run a mix of short-chat conversational traffic and long-context document summarization workloads. Typical steady-state token throughput is ~120M tokens/day; peak batch windows can spike to ~3x for product launches.
- Our SLO: p50 < 150 ms, p95 < 450 ms for chat endpoints (sequence length ~512), and batch summarization can accept p99 up to 5s.
- We asked vendors for recommended GPU families, suggested slotting (reserved vs burst), and a phased reservation plan that matches a 12-month growth runway. Please include quantization and fallback recommendations that preserve quality.

Two quick asks: can you provide a phased reservation proposal (month 0, month 3, month 6) with expected throughput per GPU class and an opinionated GPU mix (e.g., % H100 vs A100 vs L4 or equivalent)? Also, please flag any features that require Dedicated vs Private deployment.

Procurement will expect the filled questionnaire but technical answers are sufficient for now.

Ben / Lauren — see my notes below (technical summary + phased reservation recommendation). I've attached a short PDF and a CSV of estimated throughput (kTokens/sec equivalent) per GPU profile. High-level recommendations first, then rationale and numbers.

1) Recommendation (phased, pragmatic):
- Month 0 (onboarding / PoC): Reserve a small baseline pool equivalent to 8 H100-80GB slots (hot lane) + 12 A100-40GB slots (warm lane). This gives predictable low-latency for chat and cost-effective capacity for summarization.
- Month 3 (scale): Expand to 20 H100 + 30 A100. Enable burst to hosted pool for +2.5x peak capacity via shared hosted lanes.
- Month 6 (mature): Target a mixed committed pool of 40 H100 + 40 A100, keep 10% headroom as dynamic buffer and enable quantized L4-equivalents for embedding/low-cost inference.

2) GPU blend rationale:
- H100 (80GB) for high-throughput, long-context models and low-latency chat when pinned to hot lanes. Excellent perf for fp16/AMP kernels and large KV caches.
- A100 (40GB) for cost-efficient inference of medium-context models and batch summarization; good quantization path to reduce tokens/sec cost.
- L4 (or equivalent 24GB inference-optimized chips) for static embedding services and low-cost route for high-volume lightweight calls. Use these primarily for caching and rerank/embedding workloads, not primary chat.

3) Throughput estimates (simple):
- One H100-80GB slot (Redwood runtime): ~1.2k tokens/sec for seq=512 conversational workload at p95 ~350ms when continuously batched; peak burst can hit ~3k tok/s with aggressive batching in warm windows.
- One A100-40GB slot: ~700 tok/s for same profile (batching dependent), better $/token for batch summarization.
- L4-equivalent: ~2500 tok/s for short-seq embedding workloads (very cheap per token).

4) Reservation phasing (tokens/day coverage rough):
- Month 0 pool (8 H100 + 12 A100) => steady capacity ~ (8*1.2k + 12*0.7k) = ~12,000 tok/s (~1.04B tok/day) — plenty for initial workloads; primary value is latency headroom.
- Month 3 pool (20 H100 + 30 A100) => ~ (24k + 21k) = 45k tok/s steady (~3.9B tok/day) allowing comfortable handling of 3x peaks using burst lanes.
- Month 6 pool (40 H100 + 40 A100) => ~ (48k + 28k) = 76k tok/s steady (~6.6B tok/day) for sustained growth.

Notes on fallbacks & Dedicated vs Private:
- Dedicated required for strict SLA-backed latency commitments and data isolation. Private (VPC) option available if they need on-prem or HSM/KMS integration.
- Recommend canary routing: route chat traffic to hot H100 pool with A/B fallback to A100 cluster on overload. Configure automatic model-variant fallback (quantized weights) when latency budget is tight.
- Quantization: recommend 4-bit/8-bit post-training quantization for batch summarization models to improve packing and reduce committed capacity needs. Keep chat-critical models at 16-bit if quality checks show regressions.

Attached: redwood_gpu_profile_recommendation.pdf, throughput_estimates_ksps.csv

Let me know if you want me to convert these numbers into the questionnaire format or a single-page summary for procurement.
